title: 11 Days Without Sleep
lines: In {1964~nineteen sixty-four}, a seventeen-year-old stayed awake for eleven days. | No caffeine, no pills.
Randy Gardner was a high-school student in San Diego. | It was a science-fair project.
Day two: his eyes can't focus. | He can't tell objects apart by touch.
Day four: he's irritable and forgetful, | and he starts to see things that aren't there.
He even believes he's a famous American football player.
By day eleven, his speech slurs | and his memory fails. | Yet he still beats a Stanford sleep scientist at pinball.
After two hundred and sixty-four hours, he finally sleeps: | about fourteen hours.
Today, Guinness no longer accepts this record. | It's too dangerous.
What's the longest you've ever stayed awake? | Tell me in the comments.
